name: Mesa Verde
significance: Exceptional preservation of Ancestral Puebloan culture
description: Ancient Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings and archaeological sites.

name: Cahokia Mounds
significance: Largest prehistoric Native American city north of Mexico
description: Largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico, with over 120 earthen mounds.

name: Chaco Canyon
significance: Center of ceremonial, trade, and administrative activities
description: Major center of Ancestral Puebloan culture with monumental architecture and astronomical alignments.

name: Poverty Point
significance: One of North America's most impressive ancient engineering feats
description: Large prehistoric earthwork site built by the Poverty Point culture.

name: Serpent Mound
significance: Largest surviving prehistoric effigy mound in the world
description: A 1,348-foot-long prehistoric effigy mound in the shape of a serpent.

name: Hopewell Culture Site
significance: Center of extensive trade network and ceremonial activity
description: Complex of earthworks and mounds built by the Hopewell culture.

name: Taos Pueblo
significance: One of the oldest continuously inhabited communities in the United States
description: Ancient pueblo continuously inhabited for over 1,000 years.

name: Bandelier National Monument
description: Cliff dwellings and rock art of Ancestral Puebloan people in New Mexico.

name: Moundville
description: Second-largest Mississippian site in the US with 29 platform mounds.

name: Aztec Ruins
description: Misnamed ruins of an Ancestral Puebloan great house with over 400 rooms.

name: Ocmulgee Mounds
description: Ceremonial mounds and earth lodge from the Mississippian period in Georgia.

name: Effigy Mounds
description: Over 200 prehistoric mounds including animal effigy mounds in Iowa.

name: Casa Grande
description: Four-story ancient structure built by the Hohokam people in Arizona.

name: Spiro Mounds
description: Important Mississippian culture site with burial mounds and artifacts in Oklahoma.

name: Etowah Mounds
description: Major Mississippian culture site with six earthen mounds in Georgia.

name: Hovenweep
description: Six groups of Ancestral Puebloan villages with distinctive tower structures.

name: Canyon de Chelly
description: Spectacular cliff dwellings in a dramatic canyon setting in Arizona.

name: Tonto National Monument
description: Two cliff dwellings occupied by the Salado culture in Arizona.

name: Montezuma Castle
significance: One of the best-preserved cliff dwellings in North America
description: A 20-room high-rise apartment built into a limestone cliff by the Sinagua people.

name: Gila Cliff Dwellings
description: A series of caves in the Gila Wilderness containing 46 rooms built by the Mogollon people.

name: Russell Cave
significance: Continuous human use for over 10,000 years
description: A cave shelter providing one of the most complete records of prehistoric cultures in the Southeast.

name: Angel Mounds
significance: Northernmost Middle Mississippian culture civic-ceremonial center
description: A fortified town complex in Indiana serving as a regional chiefdom center.

name: Newark Earthworks
significance: Largest set of geometric earthen enclosures in the world
description: Hopewell culture earthworks including the Great Circle and Octagon Earthworks used for astronomy.

name: L'Anse aux Meadows
significance: Only confirmed Norse site in North America
description: Viking settlement in Newfoundland, evidence of the first European presence in the Americas.

name: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Cliff formation used by indigenous peoples of the Plains to hunt bison for nearly 6,000 years.

name: Wupatki
significance: Cultural crossroads of Ancient Puebloan people
description: A large 100-room pueblo dwelling near the Sunset Crater volcano in Arizona.

name: Petroglyph National Monument
significance: One of the largest petroglyph sites in North America
description: Volcanic basalt escarpment featuring over 24,000 images carved by Ancestral Puebloans.

name: Toltec Mounds
significance: Ceremonial center of the Plum Bayou culture
description: Arkansas site with 18 mounds surrounded by a 100-foot embankment, mistakenly attributed to Toltecs.

name: Fort Ancient
significance: Largest prehistoric hilltop enclosure in the US
description: Massive earthworks built by the Hopewell culture atop a bluff above the Little Miami River.

name: Dickson Mounds
description: Burial mounds and settlement site in Illinois, pivotal in the study of paleopathology.

name: Blythe Intaglios
significance: Massive geoglyphs visible from the air
description: Gigantic human and animal figures etched into the desert floor near the Colorado River.

name: Marksville
significance: Type site for the Marksville culture
description: Ceremonial center in Louisiana reflecting a southern variant of the Hopewell tradition.

name: Crystal River
significance: Long-occupied ceremonial center on Florida's coast
description: A six-mound complex with burial, temple, and midden mounds used for over 1,600 years.

name: Tuzigoot
description: A 110-room hilltop pueblo in the Verde Valley of Arizona.

name: Navajo National Monument (Betatakin)
description: Contains three large cliff dwellings: Betatakin, Keet Seel, and Inscription House.

name: Pinson Mounds
significance: Largest Middle Woodland mound complex in the US
description: A massive ceremonial center featuring 17 mounds, including Sauls Mound, the second-highest prehistoric mound in North America.

name: Old Stone Fort
description: A Middle Woodland ceremonial enclosure with walls of stone and earth, situated between the forks of the Duck River.

name: Chucalissa
significance: Best-preserved Mississippian town in the region
description: A major Walls Phase town south of Memphis featuring a central plaza, residential ridges, and a large platform mound.

name: Mound Bottom
significance: Civic-ceremonial center of the Harpeth River
description: A Mississippian complex located in a horseshoe bend of the Harpeth River, featuring at least 12 earthen mounds.

name: Shiloh Indian Mounds
description: A town of seven mounds overlooking the Tennessee River, preserved within the boundary of the Shiloh National Military Park.

name: Sellars Farm
description: A palisaded village with a large platform mound, best known for the discovery of the sandstone 'Sandy' statue.

name: Castalian Springs Mound Site
description: A mound center built around a mineral lick, famous for the discovery of the 'Castalian Springs Shell Gorget'.

name: Moccasin Bend
description: A National Archeological District preserving Paleo-Indian, Archaic, Woodland, and Mississippian habitation sites.

name: Link Farm (Duck River Cache)
significance: Source of the spectacular Duck River Cache
description: The site where 46 ceremonial flint swords and statues were discovered in 1894, one of the greatest cache finds in antiquity.

name: Obion Mounds
significance: Largest Mississippian site in West Tennessee
description: An early Mississippian site featuring seven mounds arranged around a plaza, located near the banks of the Obion River.

name: Toqua
description: A major Mississippian and later Cherokee town (now largely submerged by Tellico Lake) that was a center of trade and diplomacy.

name: Old Town (Franklin)
description: A privately owned Mississippian village and mound complex located along the Harpeth River near the ancient Natchez Trace.

name: Fewkes Group
description: A multi-mound complex located in Primm Historic Park, preserving evidence of the 'Bowling Green Phase' culture.

name: Big Bone Cave
description: A dry cave containing perfectly preserved cane torches and woven debris from prehistoric mineral mining, later used for Civil War saltpeter.

name: Swallow Bluff Island
description: A Mississippian chieftaincy located entirely on an island in the Tennessee River, featuring a primary platform mound and village.
